summary: A passage from a novel (Book 11, part 74) set around Christmas, after a Thanksgiving party at the Simpsons'. Mrs. Randall works hard for her children's future, and Rebecca recalls milestones in the year or two after the party. On Christmas morning Rebecca and her family exchange modest handmade and purchased gifts, then she receives an unexpected parcel containing a coral bead necklace with a coral rosebud cross and a card reading 'Merry Christmas from Mr. Aladdin', which she realizes comes from Mr. Ladd.
one_line: Christmas morning at Sunnybrook Farm, where Rebecca receives a mysterious coral necklace signed 'Mr. Aladdin', revealed to be from Mr. Ladd.
key_facts: Rebecca Randall's first milestone after the Simpsons' Thanksgiving party was Christmas Day.
The Christmas morning was described as fresh and crystal, with icicles hanging from the trees and pale blue glaze on the snow.
The Simpsons' red barn stood out as a glowing mass of color in the white landscape.
Rebecca had made presents for each of the seven persons at Sunnybrook Farm on an expenditure of fifty cents.
Miss Sawyer gave her niece a gray squirrel muff and tippet.
Aunt Jane made Rebecca a dress of soft green cashmere, a color like that of a young leaf.
Rebecca's mother gave her a 'tatting' collar.
Mrs. Cobb sent scarlet mittens and Emma Jane sent a handkerchief.
Rebecca made a tea-cosy with a letter 'M' in outline stitch and a frilled pincushion marked with a 'J' for her two aunts.
A boy delivered a parcel to Rebecca at breakfast time, asking if Miss Rebecca Randall lived there.
The parcel contained a case with a long chain of delicate pink coral beads ending in a cross made of coral rosebuds.
A card under the cross read 'Merry Christmas from Mr. Aladdin'.
Rebecca said under her breath that the sender was Mr. Ladd.
Miss Miranda remarked that opening the parcel would be a good way to find out who sent it.
Mrs. Randall lived in her children's future rather than her own present, as a mother often does when her own lot seems hard.
